evals.name: locates dominant leak before proposing tactics
evals.prompt: Our churn is up and I want to build a winback email flow. Retention curve: week0 100%, week1 92%, week2 61%, week4 55%, week8 52%, week12 50%.
expect: identifies the early-life leak (week1->week2 slide), not winback, as the dominant zone
refuses to design the winback flow before the leak is placed
sizes the loss in retained-customer-months, not vibes

evals.name: runs the incrementality gut-check
evals.prompt: We emailed at-risk subscribers and 28% renewed. That flow is a winner, right?
expect: asks for the counterfactual / what share would have renewed anyway
recommends a 5-10% holdout before claiming lift
declines to call the 28% renewal rate incremental lift

evals.name: flags product/pricing problems a message cannot fix
evals.prompt: Users love us in week 1 then stop logging in by week 3. Write me a re-engagement sequence.
expect: flags this as a possible value-decay / product problem, not purely a messaging one
does not immediately produce a cadence as the fix
labels claims with evidence tags where data is missing
